Subject: POC trial planning & success criteria — ZetaCorp

Hi Alice / Carlos,

Thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope, success criteria, timeline, and next steps so we have a single reference for the team. Please review and let me know any edits.

High-level scope
- 2-week evaluation of Redwood Inference for customer-facing search ranking and summarization flows
- Models: open Llama-3-13B baseline (quantized) and a tuned variant if needed
- Environment: Dedicated trial on us-west with sample dataset you provide (anonymized)

Proposed success criteria (subject to your sign-off)
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 350ms for single-request path under 20 RPS
2) Quality: Summarization ROUGE-L improvement >= 8 points vs current baseline OR human-rated relevance >= 4/5 on a 50-sample set
3) Cost: Token cost <= $0.003 per 1k tokens for production-like throughput (after batching/caching config)
4) Reliability: No more than 1% error rate during the trial window

Timeline & milestones
- Kickoff / environment setup (week 0): target Sep 20 — provision dedicated trial, upload dataset, initial tests
- Week 1: baseline runs, metric collection, tweak batching/quantization profiles
- Week 2: focused quality evals, final readout, recommendation + next-step proposal

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (PM owner), Dev (technical lead) — provisioning, model config, monitoring
- ZetaCorp: Alice (product lead), Carlos (engineering lead) — dataset, evaluation cohort, access to test environment

Next steps (action items)
- Alice: confirm success criteria and share anonymized dataset (S3 link) by Sep 17
- Carlos: confirm IP allowlist / network constraints for us-west cluster by Sep 17
- Marissa/Dev: prepare kickoff agenda + share calendar invites for Sep 20

Attachments: Zeta_POC_success_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet) — draft success criteria and sample eval plan

Happy to hop on a short call if you'd prefer to walk through the plan.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few notes/questions from our side: 

- Success criteria: the quality target sounds reasonable. For the human-rated relevance, can we do a 75-sample set instead of 50? Our PM wants slightly larger sample for confidence.
- Latency: 350ms p95 is okay as long as it's measured from our edge gateway to the inference cluster; please confirm the measurement point.
- Cost: will the $0.003/1k tokens include the cost of any tuned variants or is that baseline only?

Action items on our side
- I'll aim to share an anonymized S3 bucket with 1000 sample records (we can mark the 75 samples for human eval) by Sep 17 EOD.
- Carlos will send over our network/IP allowlist and any firewall rules by Sep 17.
- Procurement: I've looped in procurement@zetacorp.com for standard trial MSA questions — they might have a short redline.

Proposed kickoff: Sep 20 at 10:00am PT works for us. If that still works for you, please send a calendar invite.

On the cost question: can you put Dev on copy to confirm whether the quoted token cost is for baseline only or for tuned variants as well?

Thanks — looking forward to the trial.

Best,
Alice

Hi team — looping in a few technical prerequisites so the kickoff can be smooth.

Quick checklist for ZetaCorp (please confirm or let me know blockers):
- Allowlist: add these outbound IPs for the us-west cluster: 3.120.45.78, 3.120.45.79
- S3 access: provide a read-only IAM role policy or pre-signed URLs; pre-signed is easiest for a short trial
- Data format: 1 JSON per line, fields: id, text, meta (no PII in text) — sample file size ~50MB preferred for initial runs
- Auth: we'll use short-lived API keys tied to the trial account; no long-term keys are created
- Quotas: we'll set 20 RPS with burst to 40 during baseline runs — let me know if that needs tweaking

I'll prepare the initial infra provision on Sep 19 so we can test on Sep 20. Attached is a short note with network expectations (network_prereqs.txt).
